title: Lope Hurtado de Mendoza (Rome) to Charles V, 1522 — RAH Salazar 9/26, DECODE R9634–R9656

transcription.notes: Only the crib passage on f. 238 is transcribed so far; the count is of code groups aligned to the clear with exact word counts, counted by hand, not measured by _check_profile.py.

transcription.notes: DECODE records this as Non-decrypted. Two short passages on f. 262 read here; the count is of code groups resolved, counted by hand.

DECODE records this as Non-decrypted, and it has no clear version or duplicate anywhere. Used as the independent control on the key; only 'el papa' read so far. 2026-10-02: token file r9656_cipher.txt built from the 1524-notation tables of read_r9656.md; regraded to 61% read as sense. 2026-10-03: re-transcribed from the images in the R9634 notation (old file kept as r9656_cipher_1524notation.txt); 78.7% read as sense.

DECODE calls this Partially decrypted, but the leaf carries NO cipher at all - it is written entirely in the clear and signed Lope Hurtado. The 'partial' status appears to reflect faded show-through at the head of the page. Read complete as read_r9652.md; there is nothing here to decipher.

First transcribed 2026-10-02, whole cipher of ff. 14r-15v line by line (r9634_cipher.txt; r9634_tokens.txt is the cipher-only derivative that was measured; decode.py counts 1191 because it keeps the '·' marks). Mixed stream of code groups and single letter signs. Dated in the clear on f. 16r 'de Genoba xiij de setiembre 1522'; DECODE has only the month. No clear version in the record, none in CSP Spain ii.

Five cipher runs in a clear letter; transcription in read_r9646.md (code blocks), counted from those blocks, not measured by _check_profile.py. Top four lines of the image are mirrored show-through from f. 252v.

system.summary: Three-letter consonant-vowel-consonant nomenclator codes mixed inline with clear Spanish, with homophones at code level (ta and tu both = 'no'), codes used for syllables as well as whole words, and long words spelled letter by letter between the codes.
system.sibling_key: Alonso Sanchez's 1522 Venice cipher and Juan Manuel's 1522 Rome cipher, both reconstructed by Tomokiyo; same design, provably different values (xul = 'lo' here, 'despues' in Sanchez).

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo's 2025 article covers Sanchez (R9593-R9632) and Juan Manuel (R9499-R9529) only; Lope Hurtado is not mentioned and his records fall outside both ranges. A web search returns no decipherment.

conditions.human_role: redirected the session to this target; supplied the DECODE login cookie reused from an earlier target. Would need to fetch higher-resolution images from the RAH's own Biblioteca Digital, which blocks automated access, to lift the alphabet limit.

solution.what: Established in the sanchez1522 session that these nine records are not in Sanchez's cipher: his codes end strictly in b c d f g h l m n, Hurtado's take finals p and z.
Searched for a published decipherment of Hurtado's cipher. None: Tomokiyo's article covers Sanchez and Juan Manuel only and does not mention him; web search returns nothing. The key is unpublished.
Split the nine Lope Hurtado records out of sanchez1522 into their own target with images and DECODE metadata.
Found that R9644 carries both the ciphered letter (ff. 238-239) and a full contemporary clear version (f. 242), headed 'Claro' section by section and keyed to the cipher by marginal letters A, B, C.

Aligned the cipher against the clear on an exact-count run: 'ton tab xud xul y-m xon' against 'que nunca hombre lo fue mas', six tokens for six words in a sentence with no room for slippage, plus tu = no from 'no apretallo mucho'. Seven values confirmed; eleven more read as probable from the surrounding sentence where counts are not exact.

Cross-checked against the sibling keys: xul = 'lo' here but 'despues' in Sanchez, so the keys are provably distinct. None of the seven confirmed codes appears in Tomokiyo's 173-code Juan Manuel table either, which is consistent with a third key but not conclusive since that table is partial.

Second anchor on f. 238: 'zun top' immediately before the clear words 'descargo de los q', against plaintext 'da por descargo de lo que dexa'. Confirms top = por in an independent context and gives zun = da. Also shows long words spelled letter by letter between the codes (a ten-sign run where 'satisfecho' must be, an eight-sign run where 'servidor' must be). Nine values now confirmed, twelve probable, kept apart in a confidence column.

Checked R9650 f. 270 (the other Decrypted record): ton tab xud stand there in identical forms, and top again immediately precedes clear words in a slot reading 'por disimular en este caso' - a third independent context for top = por. tu and zun recur. So Hurtado used one key across these letters and values won on R9644 carry to the rest, which is what makes the six non-decrypted records reachable.

Found the start of the clear version on f. 241 ('Al Rey - de Lope Hurtado, de Roma, del primero de noviembre', then Claro, then lettered sections), so the clear runs ff. 241-242 and covers the cipher of ff. 238-239 from its start.

Aligned the stretch after the clear words 'si algo se le dixesse': cipher '<8-sign run> ton [b]z7 teg' against plaintext 'pensaria que era para'. New confirmed values era and para, plus the letter r attested twice (the r of the spelled pensaria, and zun+r = dar, which re-confirms zun = da). Thirteen confirmed, thirteen probable.

Retracted an earlier probable value: zar = 'Bari' was wrong. zar is frequent and falls here in the slot 'los criados de su Sa'; it is now carried as 'de' or 'su', still probable. The confirmed/probable split in key_codes.tsv is what caught this - no probable value had been used to derive anything.

A line of R9644 f. 238 aligned end to end with the plaintext, nothing left over: 'ta xil+s zun+z xur zun q x-i-r-i-a ton tu ton+ria ton xul' = 'no les dar nada y diria que no queria que lo'. Gives ta = no (a homophone of tu, both in the same line, so the cipher has homophones at code level), xil = le, q = y, and the ending -ria. Shows codes carrying syllables: xur+zun = na+da, ton+ria = que+ria, with zun the same 'da' confirmed earlier in 'da por'. Nineteen confirmed, thirteen probable.

ton+zun+ria-n = que+da+rian = 'quedarian' on R9644 f. 238 against the plaintext. Three codes chained into one word. zun = da now confirmed in three distinct roles: a whole word (da por), the second syllable of na-da, and the middle syllable of que-da-rian. The ending gives the letter 4 = n, matching the n of the spelled pensaria. Twenty-one confirmed, thirteen probable.

Exact-count run at the end of the paragraph: four cipher units for 'tiene perdida la esperança'. 'perdida' is spelled out, seven signs for seven letters, which hands over a first slice of the substitution alphabet: p, e, r, d (two different signs), i, a, and n. Cross-checks against the spelled 'pensaria' earlier and against r, already confirmed twice. Thirty-one confirmed, thirteen probable. One sign left unassigned: it reads t in 'tiene' but seemed s in 'pensaria', so one transcription is wrong and it is not guessed.

Pushed a profile.json with a non-schema field (system.homophones.note) which made _check_profile.py report INVALID; caught on the next check and fixed in the following commit. The homophone observation (two codes for 'no'; two signs for the letter d inside the spelled 'perdida') is kept in NOTES.md, where prose belongs, and recorded in the schema as max_per_consonant = 2.

'El camarero Pedro es el principal' in the clear gives the spelled name Pedro on the cipher side: five signs for five letters, p/e/d/r already confirmed, so m = o falls out. Alphabet so far: p, e, r, d (two signs), i, a, n, o. Thirty-three confirmed, fourteen probable.

Found that R9648 (Non-decrypted) carries the same matter as R9644's clear - 'pregunte a su S.' and 'le avia embiado la carta de v. Mt y q esperava saber lo de Yngalaterra' stand in the clear on its leaves, answering to section C of the R9644 plaintext. Hurtado sent his despatches in duplicate, so one clear version serves both, and R9644's plaintext cribs R9648 as well.

First previously-unread text read: R9648 f. 262, nine cipher tokens against nine plaintext words with nothing left over - 'y que el papa no esta en que venga' - and 'que nueva tenia de Francia' after the clear words 'pregunte a su S.'. The values q=y, ton=que and tu=no, won on R9644, reappear here correctly, which is the check that matters. Seven new values: taf=papa, y-of=esta, y-uc=en, te-r=nueva, tenia, y-on=Francia, and the spelled 'venga'; y-ub=el promoted from probable. Short, and leaning on the duplicate's plaintext rather than the key alone, so a foothold rather than a reading.

More of R9648 f. 262 reads: 'ton y-ub zed' before the clear 'le avia embiado la carta' = 'que el arcobispo', giving zed = arcobispo, a name-code for the archbishop of Bari. And a continuous run 'la paz por los infieles y por la necessidad', where la, por, los and y are all values won earlier and reappearing correctly, and tef = paz is new. Forty-six confirmed, eleven probable.

The alphabet decodes a word on its own. On R9648 f. 264, between the clear words 'antes de agora' and 'si se oviera hecho', the cipher gives 'tu su <run> <8-sign run> xur zun' = 'no se [h]uviera perdido nada'. The eight-sign run spells p-e-r-d-i-d-o, and six of those signs (e, r, d, i, d, o) were derived on R9644 from 'perdida', 'pensaria' and 'Pedro' - every one correct here in a word decoded without being looked for. xur+zun = na+da reappears intact. R9644 carries the same sentence in the clear, being the duplicate, so the reading is corroborated rather than unsupported; but the decoding was done from the key, not read off the crib.

THE VALIDATION THAT MATTERS. Everything so far leaned somewhere on R9644's plaintext, R9648 being its duplicate. R9656 (ff. 334-335, headed 'De Lope Hurtado de xx de noviembre') is a different despatch three weeks later with no clear version and no duplicate. The key reads there unaided: after the clear words 'las cartas traxo don Correo q vino con la valante', the cipher gives '|| tu n7 <2 runs> y-ub taf' = 'no ... EL PAPA', with y-ub = el and taf = papa both won on R9648 against R9644's crib. Elsewhere on the leaf ton, zar, y-of, sub and tu all fall in slots that make sense. The three unresolved units are left blank rather than guessed.

R9648 f. 264 after the clear 'A lo q he entendido': 'zil y-ub zed zar <spelled Cosenza>' against section B of the R9644 plaintext = 'con el arcobispo de Cosenza'. Gives zil = con, re-confirms zed = arcobispo in a second context, and promotes zar = de, now attested three times (de su Sa, de Francia, de Cosenza) - which matters because zar is one of the commonest groups on every leaf. Forty-nine confirmed, ten probable.

rab = vuestra magestad, from 'zar rab' falling exactly on 'de v. ma' in section C, and from rab being one of the commonest groups on every leaf - which is what 'vuestra magestad' should be in despatches to the Emperor. The spelled words either side check the alphabet again: 'honrrado' and 'approvechado' both end a-d-o, with n inside the first, every sign having come from R9644. Fifty confirmed, ten probable.

Attempted to extend the substitution alphabet from spelled words with known plaintext (Cosenza, venga, tiene, pensaria). Blocked: the transcriptions contradict each other - tiene wants one sign = t where pensaria wants it = s; venga wants a sign = v where perdida fixes it = i; Cosenza comes out eight signs for seven letters with two signs apparently doing double duty. At least one transcription in each pair is wrong, so those signs are left unassigned rather than picking whichever suits. Same wall as sanchez1522: the three-letter code groups read off the page easily, the spelled letter-signs need a picture-book built glyph by glyph against known plaintext.

Section A of R9644 (f. 237, marked A in the margin) aligned against its clear on f. 241. Six values already fixed - tu (no), xul (lo), ton (que), y-af (es), zil (con), rab (vuestra magestad) - all fall in their right places across one long sentence, the densest single check the key has had. New: su-su = 'su' and s-id = 'Sa' (Su Santidad, the Pope), from the pair standing at 'su Sa' in 'prevenga a su Sa'. Three more probable: obligado, haga, dezir. Fifty-two confirmed, twelve probable.

Paragraph 2 of R9644 f. 237 against its clear: 'porque su Sa tenia tanta passion que no conocia lo que don Joan'. Seven fixed values in a row (top, ton, s-id, ton, tu, zil, xul, ton), plus another instance of the stem-plus-ending pattern - zil (con) + spelled 'ocia' = 'conocia', the third construction zil has appeared in. Three new probables: tenia, tanta, don. Noted but not settled: s-id stood beside su-su (su) as 'su Sa' in section A but carries 'su Sa' alone here, so either it means Sa with su sometimes coded separately, or it means the whole title.

End of R9644 f. 237 against 'lo que le parece del duque ... lo que no quedo de don Joan segun dizen todos'. Gives y-o-b = duque (the Duke of Sessa, imperial ambassador at Rome); zar+one sign = del; ton+d+o = 'quedo', a code finished with two alphabet signs; and d-o-n spelled outright, which fixes a second sign for o beside m. That last matters beyond the word: this sign was one of those whose readings contradicted each other, and it turns out to be a homophone, so part of the earlier alphabet tangle was a missing homophone rather than a bad transcription. Fifty-five confirmed, thirteen probable.

Built decode.py, which applies only confirmed values (probables print in angle brackets, unknowns as ?tok) and reports coverage. Measured on two lines from records the key was not built on: R9650 f. 270 gives 8/13 = 62%, R9648 f. 262 gives 7/10 = 70%. So roughly two tokens in three resolve on sight in letters the crib does not cover. The misses are a few unmet nomenclator codes and the spelled runs, which need the alphabet. Good enough to follow the sense of a passage, not good enough to edit one.

Found that R9650 also has its own full clear version, on f. 272, headed 'Al Rey - De Lope Hurtado de ...' exactly as R9644's. So there are TWO complete cribs covering two different letters. R9650's brings vocabulary the first lacks - franceses, Italia, dinero, Leon, yglesia, Hieronymo Adorno, don Joan Manuel, visorey de Napoles, posta - which are exactly the content nouns the key is short of. It also gives the letters' subject independently of the cipher: the French determined to come into Italy and sending a great sum of money to Lyon, the Pope to do what he can, Adorno having intercepted letters, the archbishop of Bari the channel to the Emperor.

R9650 f. 269 (the cipher whose clear is f. 272) against 'que los franceses son determinados de venir en Italia, y enbian gran suma de dinero a Leon, y que es menester'. Eight placements of already-fixed values land correctly in one sentence of a letter the first crib does not cover - ton, zar three times, y-uc, q twice, y-af, xul. The slots give the content nouns the key was short of, recorded as probable since token counts are not exact: franceses, Italia, dinero, Leon, gran, suma. Sixty-one entries, fifty-five confirmed.

R9650 f. 269 against 'y que el papa haga lo que pudiere': six fixed values (q, ton, y-ub, taf, xul, ton) round a single unknown, which the sense fixes as haga - promoted from probable, having been in the same slot in R9644 section A ('no haga lo que es obligado'). A value turning up twice in the same construction across two different letters is not coincidence. zar rab = 'de v. ma' again at the end of the line. Fifty-six confirmed.

R9650 f. 269 against 'y por lo que deve, no se ponga en esto': seven fixed values in one short clause (q, top, xul, ton, zar, tu, su, y-uc). New probables from the gaps: deve, ponga, esto, and cartas from the phrase before. Sixty-five entries, fifty-six confirmed.

Consolidation audit of the key: cross-checked every value for two codes claiming the same plaintext. Four retractions, kept in the file as commented RETRACTED lines rather than deleted - zed='de' (superseded by zed=arcobispo, confirmed twice), the sign-pair='el' (early non-exact alignment; el is y-ub, confirmed three times), one 'tenia' (conflicts with the confirmed one; one transcription is wrong), and one 'nada' (a misreading of xur+zun). The only surviving multi-claims are genuine homophones, each confirmed in evidence: two codes for 'no', two signs for d, two signs for o.

Read R9644 and R9650 complete, from the clerks' own contemporary clear versions (ff. 241-242 and f. 272), transcribed from the images into read_r9644.md and read_r9650.md. R9648 is R9644's duplicate so the same clear reads it too. Three of the nine records now have their content read in full; the ciphered leaves of those letters are read in part against the same text.

R9652 read complete: it carries NO cipher. DECODE calls it 'Partially decrypted' but the leaf is written entirely in the clear and signed Lope Hurtado; the status appears to reflect faded show-through at the head. Content: the licenciado Bernardino, a 'gran bellaco' the Duke of Sessa wants arrested, and Adrian VI declining a night arrest in Rome while offering a formal suplicacion instead; plus the viceroy of Naples' despatch on the siege of Rhodes forwarded to the Emperor. That last ties this correspondence to Sanchez's R9653 of 20 Nov, which carries the Rhodes news from Venice - Rome and Venice reporting the same disaster in the same fortnight, in two different ciphers, bound in the same volume.

Measured the key on R9645, a record with no crib of any kind: 57% of tokens resolve with confirmed values only. It decodes to 'se si no con [...] con vuestra magestad, que no [...] en [...] esta[do] [...] de vuestra magestad' - the shape and subject of the sentence with the content words missing. That is the honest ceiling of the present key on an uncribbed letter: function words and names resolve, spelled content words do not.

CORRECTION. An 8x zoom on the spelled 'perdido' in R9648 f. 264 shows the word resolving into seven distinct glyphs, but with the signs in positions 2 and 6 - which must be e and d - looking near-identical. They had been read as different letters at the lower zoom the alphabet values were taken at. So the nine alphabet values were labelled 'confirmed' on weaker evidence than that word implies. All ten sign entries downgraded to probable, with the reason written into each row; decode.py now shows every alphabet value in angle brackets. The distinction the earlier audit should have drawn: code groups are written as ordinary latin trigrams, legible without paleographic judgement and cross-checking against each other, so the 47 of them stand; alphabet signs rest on discriminating cursive shapes at the limit of the scans and do not.

Re-measured coverage after the downgrade, with decode.py applying confirmed values only: R9650 f. 270 still 62%. The coverage figures were carried almost entirely by the code groups, so the downgrade does not move them - which is itself the evidence that the nomenclator and the alphabet are independent, and that the reading rests on the safe half.

Established what would actually finish this, and that it needs the human. DECODE serves these leaves at 3440x2465 for a TWO-PAGE opening - about 1700 px across a folio, enough for the latin trigrams and not enough to tell two similar cursive signs apart. That is the measured cause of the alphabet limit. The volume is in the Coleccion Salazar y Castro, which the RAH is digitising at bibliotecadigital.rah.es; those images would be far better than DECODE's derivative copies. But that site returns HTTP 403 to automated requests and puts a bot check in front of its search, so it needs Daniel to fetch, exactly as DECODE's image server needs his logged-in cookie. Searching there for 'Salazar y Castro, A-26' and pulling ff. 237-243, 260-272, 334-335 at full resolution would unblock the alphabet and with it the five uncribbed records.

Checked whether DECODE holds anything better, using the logged-in cookie. It does not. The full-size file filesrv returns IS the 3440x2465 two-page opening already fetched (1.45 MB); MASTER_, MS_, ORIG_ and .tif variants all come back as the server's 5,244-byte not-found placeholder. The Image Manager (/decrypt-web/ImagesList) answers 'You do not have permission to access' with this cookie - it is a viewer session, not an editor one, so its zoom view is unreachable too. The ceiling is DECODE's stored derivative copy, which confirms that lifting the alphabet limit needs the RAH's own digitisation rather than anything further from DECODE.

Walked f. 239, the third ciphered leaf, marked B/C/D in the margin. Section B against 'que sin el no hay nada, y con el' gives su-b-r = 'sin' (sub 'si' plus one sign) and xur+zun = nada again. Section C against 'da senal de paz ... el Rey de Francia ... por enbiar embaxador a su Sa ... pues queda de la guerra' gives tel = 'pues', confirmed by an exact slot and immediately followed by ton+zun = que+da = 'queda', which confirms both a further time; ta-r = Rey and y-ed = embaxador recorded as probable. Eighty entries, forty-nine confirmed code values.

CORRECTION to an overstatement. Measured R9656, the uncribbed control, at 42% - lower than R9645's 57% - and its output is fragments ('no ... el papa ... la ... que ... su el papa'), not substance. I had been describing the five uncribbed records as reading 'in substance'; measured, they do not. The honest ceiling on an uncribbed letter is roughly half the tokens, concentrated in function words and names, with the content words as the misses: enough to say what a passage is about when surrounding clear text helps, not enough to read one. R9648 and R9650 score higher partly because their cribs were walked. Corrected in NOTES.md, profile.json and the write-up.

Applied the 1524 alphabet (targets/lopehurtado1523/key_1524.tsv) back to the 1522 letters by re-reading R9656 f. 334 (uncribbed) off the image in 1524 notation. 'xug ∠84αx7 zar ε&∂ yun ʒ∂' = 'la venida de los franceses' on an exact count, with 1524 values a/e/n/l/i and codes zar, xug, yun unchanged; the phrase recurs on l.1-2 and 'sub ∠α84..' = 'si vien-' is echoed by the clear 'si vienen franceses'. New sign ∠ = v. Shows the 1522 and 1524 alphabets are one; the 1522 'L = i' was a transcription collision.

Checked the NOTES claim that R9634, R9646 and R9649 were never attempted. Out of date for two: read_r9646.md and read_r9649.md already existed from an earlier session that did not update NOTES or the profile. R9649 is not uncribbed either: f. 268r is the clerk's clear of the whole letter. Only R9634 was untouched.

Transcribed the whole cipher of R9634 (ff. 14r-15v, 75 manuscript lines) from the three DECODE openings at 1.5x crops, in the 1524 sign names plus the R9646/R9649 names, appending line by line to r9634_cipher.txt. 1174 symbols measured (r9634_tokens.txt). The date and place (Genoa, 13 Sept 1522) come from the clear close on f. 16r.

Applied the merged 1524 key (lopehurtado1523/key_merged.tsv), the 1522 code groups and the R9649/R9646 sign values to R9634 with a new letter mode of decode.py. Coverage 77% confirmed, 92% with probable values on the first pass; the function-word spine and the alphabet read unchanged (seiscientos hombres de armas, tomarle esto que estava en su mano, del mundo).

Read R9634 line by line (r9634_reading.tsv). Context forced new values: ɋ = r (tierra x3, 'una tierra fertil' exact), z after a code = plural s (xul z los, xud z hombres, xob z yal z grandes exercitos), yob = ducado ('lxx U yob z' = 70,000 ducats after 'serian menester cada mes'), xep = mar ('los de la xep y los de la tierra'), xu = gente ('la xu darmas'; conflicts the 1524 xu = ha-), zar∂ = des- (destruir). Content: Geronimo Adorno's plan for Charles V and Henry VIII to invade France through Provence, 600 men-at-arms and 70,000 ducats a month, in March, kept secret.

Hypothesis that the groups standing right after the run opener Ꮒ are nulls: ʃta, ɡʇo/ɣ̊ʇ/ʑto, ʆ∂, yt, yω. Tested against the one crib that covers such a run (R9649 f. 268: nothing for 'Ꮒ yω ʃta') and against sentence closure in R9634 (14r13, 14v07, 14v14, 14v17, 15r20, 15v07) and R9646 (runs 4 and 5). Holds in every context; ʃta confirmed, the others probable.

Measured R9634: 842 of 1191 cipher tokens in words read as sense = 71% (f.14r 74%, f.14v 63%, f.15r 77%, f.15v 66%); lm.best_language on the read text returns es-modern first. Valued by the key 80% confirmed / 94% with probable, so about a quarter of tokens carry values but do not form words: spelled words with one sign at the 8/ϑ, ∂ s/p/t or ε l/g limit, and about 45 codes seen once.

Retried R9646 at 1.5x: run 4 'o-i-e-se' is 'o-v-i-e-se' = oviese (second sign ∠, not α); 'Ꮒ ʃta' and 'Ꮒ ʑto ɡto' are opener + nulls; 'sed z' = sus with the plural z. Re-counted 121 tokens (not 118) and measured 97 read as sense = 80%. ʙ∠89&Ho, zip, zob, δ8ǝtoo, ʃof and the close ʙ∠47 ɣ?8δHo still fail.
Measured R9649 against its own clear (f. 268): 89/89 tokens read as sense once yω ʃta are taken as nulls. Probable values inside it: ti, ϭ, ♀, ⅋, ƀ.

Looked for a crib for R9634 and R9646 in CSP Spain ii (Bergenroth): the 2026-09-21 full-text search found no Hurtado letter of Sept-Nov 1522 calendared, so neither has a printed summary; no clear version in either record. Failed as a crib source.

Re-transcribed R9645 (f. 243r all 17 lines, f. 243v ll. 1-10) from the DECODE images at 1.5x in the R9634 notation into r9645_cipher.txt; glossed lines 13-21 converted from the 2026-09-21 pass. 489 tokens. Checked the facing f. 242v 'Claro': it is the end of R9644's clear (Ostia fortress), no crib here.

Applied key_1522_r9634.tsv plus the merged 1524 key to R9645. The unglossed f. 243r now reads as the terms of Adrian VI's capitulation with Ferrara: assiento con el duque de Ferrara (m̶8ɋ7ɣ̊Ho), tres condiciones, del feudo que el papa Alexandro, cient hombres de armas, confederarse si no con su Sd e con V. Mt., recoger deservidores. Valued 84% confirmed / 98% with probable.

Tested the null-after-Ꮒ hypothesis on R9645's contemporary glosses: the glossator writes nothing for 'Ꮒ ɣto' before yi = dize, nor for 'Ꮒ ɣto ʃta' between 'la gente de v. mgd' and 'no'. ɣto upgraded to confirmed; the earlier guess 'hasta agora' for this run is withdrawn. The gloss 'al duque de Albania' sits over yib (duque), resolving the old yub = duque conflict as a misread; 'la gente' over 'xup xu' confirms xu = gente.
Measured R9645: 358 of 489 tokens read as sense = 73% (f. 243r 70%, f. 243v 77%), against 57% confirmed coverage / about 47% read on 2026-09-21.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt by aligning the cipher of R9644 (ff. 238-239) with the clerk's full contemporary clear version bound in the same record (ff. 241-242, 'Claro', keyed by marginal letters A-C), then with the second clear version in R9650 (f. 272); the 1524 alphabet from lopehurtado1523 (itself rebuilt here) was applied back only as a later check.
outcome.notes: Unpublished cipher, opened 2026-09-20. TWO records carry the clerk's own full contemporary clear version - R9644 (ff. 241-242, in lettered sections keyed to the cipher) and R9650 (f. 272) - and R9648 is R9644's duplicate. R9652 carries no cipher at all - DECODE's 'partially decrypted' is wrong, the leaf is entirely in the clear - and is read complete too. Those four letters are therefore READ COMPLETE as to content (read_r9644.md, read_r9650.md): the Pope Adrian VI temporising between Charles V and Francis I, the French resolved to come into Italy with a great sum of money to Lyon, Hieronymo Adorno's intercepted letters, the Pope's parsimony and his unpaid household, the peace track through the archbishop of Bari. The CIPHER is read in part: 47 CODE values fixed against that plaintext and 29 probable (the 10 substitution-alphabet signs were downgraded to probable on 20 Sept after an 8x zoom showed signs that must be different letters looking near-identical at the zoom they were read at; the code groups, being plain latin trigrams that cross-check, are unaffected), kept apart in a confidence column and audited for conflicts. The key reads outside its own evidence - two thirds of tokens on sight in R9648 and R9650, and 'el papa' unaided in R9656, which has no clear version and no duplicate. Open: the five records with no clear version (R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656), and a word-perfect edition of any ciphered leaf, which needs the substitution alphabet - all ten alphabet signs probable after the 8x zoom on perdido, the rest limited by per-glyph discrimination on these scans. 2026-10-02: R9634 (Genoa, 13 Sept 1522, Adorno's Provence plan) transcribed and read in part, 71% of tokens measured; R9646 80%; R9649 read in full from its own clear f. 268 (it had been listed as uncribbed). New: ɋ = r, plural z after codes, yob ducado, xu gente, nulls after the opener Ꮒ (ʃta confirmed). Retry 2026-10-02: R9645 73% (re-transcribed, f. 243r = Ferrara capitulation terms), R9656 61% (regraded), R9634 71%; ɣto null and xu = gente confirmed on R9645's glosses. 2026-10-03: fraction_read 0.74 = tokens read as sense over the five measured uncribbed-or-own-clear letters R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656 (1557/2104); the cribbed R9644/R9648/R9650 are read complete as to content via their clear versions. 2026-10-03 (later): R9656 re-transcribed, 61% -> 79%; fraction_read 0.76 (1603/2115 over the five measured letters).

texts.label: R9644, Rome, 1 Nov 1522 (ff. 237-243), with its duplicate R9648 (9 Nov, ff. 260-265)

reading_review.note: read_r9644.md is the clerk's contemporary clear version (ff. 241-242) transcribed as continuous Spanish, sections A-C, abbreviations expanded; it reads complete. It is the reading of the cipher of R9644 and its duplicate R9648, whose ciphered leaves are not token-transcribed.

texts.summary: Hurtado's running account of Adrian VI: the Pope's good will but unsatisfying deeds, his parsimony while he waits for the archbishop of Bari, the payment of the papal household before the other side buys it, the French King's request for a safe-conduct for an ambassador, and a leak of letters shown in copy in Castile. Read from the clerk's contemporary clear version (ff. 241-242); no full transcription of the ciphered leaves was made, only the passages aligned in NOTES.md.

texts.label: R9650, Rome, Nov 1522 (ff. 269-272)

reading_review.note: read_r9650.md is the contemporary clear version transcribed as continuous Spanish; it reads as sentences with few holes.

texts.summary: The French are resolved to come into Italy and send a great sum of money to Lyon; Hieronymo Adorno has intercepted letters; the Pope, urged to act, answers lukewarmly and will not declare himself. Read from the clerk's clear version on f. 272; the ciphered leaves (ff. 269-271) are transcribed only in the passages aligned in NOTES.md.

texts.label: R9652, Rome, Nov 1522 (ff. 295-296), wholly in clear

reading_review.note: read_r9652.md: a letter wholly in clear, transcribed as continuous Spanish; no cipher.

texts.summary: A letter entirely in clear: the licenciado Bernardino, a 'gran bellaco', has turned up in Rome and Adrian VI declines a night arrest in the city; the viceroy of Naples' news of the siege of Rhodes is forwarded in copy.

texts.label: R9634, Genoa, 13 Sept 1522 (ff. 14-16)
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b13; texts/R9634_reading.md, texts/R9634_en.md): the line readings written out as continuous text with the f. 14r clear opening; clean share 0.506, carried by the clear; holes in most cipher sentences (about 45 codes seen once, the spelled place names of 14r12, 14v03). Blockers: no-key-material, needs-physical-access.
texts.summary: Four months after the imperial sack of Genoa, Hurtado reports a plan put to him by Geronimo Adorno: the Emperor and the King of England should make war on the King of France through Provence, his weakest land, with six hundred men-at-arms, light horse and soldiers at 70,000 ducats a month, settled now for March; an early form of the 1524 Provence invasion.

texts.label: R9646, Rome, [Nov 1522] (f. 252r)
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b13; texts/R9646_reading.md, texts/R9646_en.md, texts/R9634-R9656_reread_log.md): clean share 0.727 on the whole letter, carried by the clear; of the five cipher runs, 1-3 read (the Pope concerted with Ferrara, en lo de la [?decima]); run 4 (abia miedo que oviese de [...] en [...]) and run 5 (ofrecer [...] al papa para sus necesidades ... por dinero [?hara] toda [...]) keep their holes, so what the Pope feared and what was to be offered are lost. Blockers: no-key-material (zip, zob, ʃof seen once) and needs-physical-access (an unkeyed looped sign opens ð∠89&Ho and ð∠47; DECODE has no larger image, the RAH library is behind a bot check).
texts.summary: Adrian VI has concluded his settlement with Alfonso d'Este, duke of Ferrara, and a copy of the capitulation is being sent; Charles's request meets papal caution, and the archbishop [of Bari] advises an offer of money for the Pope's needs.

texts.label: R9649, Rome, 9 Nov 1522 (ff. 266-268)

reading_review.note: read_r9649.md: the three cipher runs decode word for word against the clerk's clear version on f. 268 (como el Cardenal de Santa Cruz le mata por Ostia; que el licenciado Bernardino); 89 of 89 tokens read.

texts.summary: Adrian VI asks Charles V to write urging him to garrison Ostia and give the fortress to no one, since Cardinal Santa Cruz (Carvajal) presses for it by seniority; the licenciado Bernardino has landed from Barcelona and hides at his brother's house. The cipher runs are read against the contemporary clear version on f. 268.

texts.label: R9645, Rome, Nov 1522 (ff. 243-244)
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b13; texts/R9645_reading.md, texts/R9645_en.md, texts/R9645_corrections.tsv): clean share 0.528. f. 243r now reads to l. 12 (que abia tomado assiento con el duque de Ferrara; the feudo Alexander VI [?solto] con el [?casamiento] de su [?fija]; no league con [?ningun] [?principe] ni [?señoria] save the Pope and the Emperor); r13-r17 and upper f. 243v break on #ʇʇHoε97, xωt74, tec, zuf, ʃen, ɣ7∠8ϑ9Ho, tep, 8&ɣ̊98, ϑωε7ϙ. Blockers: no-key-material, needs-physical-access.
texts.summary: The terms of Adrian VI's capitulation with Alfonso d'Este, duke of Ferrara (the feudal dues, service to the Church, no confederation except with the Pope and the Emperor, no harbouring of disservants), then news of the duke's men and the Pope; f. 243r has no gloss and the reading rests on the key.

texts.label: R9656, Rome, Nov 1522 (ff. 334-335)
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b13; texts/R9656_reading.md, texts/R9656_en.md, texts/R9656_corrections.tsv): clean share 0.564. f. 334v now reads (lo de [?Ostia]: &δϑα7 o-s-t-i-a; y como [?assi] se [?tomaran]; the Don Juan sentence in full); f. 334r ll. 4-6 and 13-17 still break on ɲ4∠&ɣ̊t, ɣαδ8, teɡ∂ ϯ∠8ɣ̊oo, ϙ8, 8x&, ßϑ7 and code 30. texts.summary: The archbishop of Bari wrote no certain news of the coming of the French; the Pope will not fail the Emperor and is content for peace, but is very suspicious that Don Juan [Manuel] was ordered from there to do what he has done. A faded contemporary clear copy on f. 335r supports part of the reading.
